in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the children you're inquiring about:**

1. **How many children do you have** that you'd like me to assess?
2. **What are their names and ages?**

Child Benefit eligibility depends on several factors, including:
- The child's age (the main factor)
- Your residency and working status in the UK
- Whether the child is in education or training (for those aged 16-19)

Please provide the names and dates of birth (or just ages) for each child you'd like me to check, and I'll guide you through the eligibility questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me work through the eligibility assessment for Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For young people in this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in **approved education or training**.

**Let me ask you: Is Alex currently in full-time education or undertaking an approved training course?**

For context, this includes:
- Full-time study at school, college, or university (like A-levels, apprenticeships, or university courses)
- Other approved training schemes

Please let me know if Alex is in any of these situations, or if he's working full-time or doing something else.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's very helpful. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education (studying A-levels), he potentially qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I need to check a few more important factors about your situation to determine your eligibility to claim Child Benefit for Alex:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in education, so let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to verify that Alex's A-level course meets the requirements:

**Is Alex studying A-levels on a full-time basis?** By full-time, I mean he's doing at least 12 hours per week of supervised study at the sixth form college (this is almost always the case with A-level students).

Also, just to confirm - **is Alex married?** (If he is, I'll need to check if he's financially dependent on you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time - it's a typical A-level course at sixth form, so definitely more than 12 hours a week. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex's full-time A-level study clearly meets the approved education requirements. Now let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to know about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is in full-time education, even if he does have a part-time job, as long as it's under 24 hours per week, this wouldn't affect his eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's helpful. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me ask about Alex's benefits:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship:

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?** (It sounds like he's doing standard A-levels, so I expect the answer is no, but let me confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - just doing his A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Now I've confirmed that Alex meets all the child-related eligibility criteria. Let me continue by checking your personal circumstances as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Please tell me about your residency:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the main residency requirement)

If you don't normally live in the UK, I can check other possibilities, such as:
- Whether you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Whether you're a Crown servant living abroad
- Other special circumstances

What's your current residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's great. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex:

**Can you confirm that you are responsible for Alex?** 

Based on what you've already told me, you live with Alex at home, which means you definitely meet the responsibility requirement. I just need to confirm this:

- **Do you live with Alex and contribute to his upkeep** (e.g., providing food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me and I provide everything for him - his food, clothes, housing, all his day-to-day needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That clearly establishes your responsibility for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important point about other potential claimants:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else likely to claim?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) currently claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Could there be anyone else who might also claim for Alex?

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time, so I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- Is he living at home with you normally?
- Or is he in hospital, residential care, or a fostering arrangement?

Based on what you've told me so far, I expect he's living at home with you, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's living at home with me - just a normal living situation, nothing unusual.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check one final important detail:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

This would only apply in specific situations, such as if Alex were in local authority care. But since you've said he's living at home with you and you're providing all his needs, I expect the answer is no.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need to provide you with your eligibility decision.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **✅ ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

---

### **Why You're Eligible:**

Alex meets all the requirements as a qualifying child:
- ✓ He's 18 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form)
- ✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week
- ✓ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✓ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

You also meet all the claimant requirements:
- ✓ You normally live in the UK
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex (living with him and providing his upkeep)
- ✓ You're the sole claimant for him
- ✓ The local council is not paying towards his care

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. Visit: [https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)

### **Important Notes:**

- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may still be eligible to claim, but you could be liable for the High Income Child Benefit Charge. This is worth checking if applicable to your situation.
- **Payment frequency**: Child Benefit is normally paid every 4 weeks (or weekly in some circumstances)

---

**Congratulations! You're eligible to claim. The next step is to submit your application to HMRC.**
